title: Welcoming the Migrants
paragraphs: When the migrants from Makkah were arriving in Madinah with almost nothing, having left their homes and businesses behind, the local residents were opening their own houses and sharing their wealth without hesitation.
One resident famously offered to divide his entire property equally with a new arrival, an offer the migrant gratefully declined, asking instead only to be shown the way to the local market.

This spirit of sharing, later described as brotherhood between the two communities, became a model that historians still study when discussing how newcomers can be successfully welcomed into an existing community.
Within a short time, the migrants had rebuilt their livelihoods, largely because the local community treated their arrival as a shared responsibility rather than a burden to manage alone.
